summary:
The bill, cited as the “Securing Community Upgrades for a Resilient Grid Act” or the “SECURE Grid Act,” amends section 366 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) (42 U.S.C. 6326) to require States to integrate the physical security, cybersecurity, and resilience of local distribution systems into their State energy security plans. The legislation does not appropriate funds; it primarily restructures and expands existing statutory planning requirements and assistance duties.

Section 2 amends EPCA section 366 in several respects. It adds a new definition in subsection (a)(3) for “local distribution system,” meaning energy infrastructure owned and operated by an electric utility at a voltage of 100 kilovolts or less. Subsection (b)(2) is revised to require that, in developing a State energy security plan, the State must consult not only owners and operators of energy infrastructure but also “suppliers of equipment for the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity.” Subsection (c) is amended to rewrite plan-content elements: paragraph (3) now more granularly requires plans to address physical threats (weather-related threats, physical attacks on local distribution systems and the bulk-power system, and supply chain risks for generation, transmission, and distribution equipment) and cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities, including threats to local distribution systems that may impact the bulk-power system. Paragraph (5) is revised to require a risk-mitigation approach that enhances reliability and end-use resilience, encompassing methods for responding to, mitigating, and recovering from the hazards described in paragraph (3).

Subsection (d)(3) is amended to insert a new subparagraph (B) that adds “supplying equipment for the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity” to the entities covered by that provision; existing subparagraph (B) is redesignated as subparagraph (C). In subsection (e), the amendment restructures the text: it designates the existing eligibility condition as paragraph (1) (“Submission required”) and adds a new paragraph (2) (“State determination”) providing that a submission under paragraph (1) “is not required to be approved by the Secretary.” This eliminates the requirement for Secretarial approval of a State’s energy security plan as a condition of eligibility. Subsection (f) is amended by striking “may” and inserting “shall,” converting the Secretary’s authority to provide assistance to States from discretionary to mandatory. Subsection (h) is amended to extend its confidentiality protections to information relating to local distribution systems. Subsection (i) is struck and replaced with a new sunset provision: “This section shall expire on September 30, 2031.”

Section 3 directs the Comptroller General to submit a report to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources not later than September 30, 2030. The report must evaluate the efficacy of State energy security plans; make recommendations to improve State risk-identification and -mitigation and to enhance the Secretary of Energy’s coordination with States; provide data on federal financial assistance under part D of title III of EPCA (42 U.S.C. 6321 et seq.) used to implement the plans and on State activities funded therewith; analyze the efficacy of the implementation of the amended section 366; and detail State use of assistance under section 366(f) and any resulting plan revisions. Any information protected from disclosure under section 366(h) must be placed in a non-public annex. The term “State energy security plan” is defined by reference to section 366(a).
